title: Operating systems
blurb: How programs run on the machine, the core ideas of operating systems, and how today's Linux schedules, manages memory, does I/O and isolates workloads.

main.title: CMU 15-213: Introduction to Computer Systems
main.why: How C becomes machine code, and what memory, linking, processes and I/O look like to a program. In English.

main.title: MIT 6.1810: Operating System Engineering
main.why: Page tables, system calls, page faults, locking, thread switching and file systems, each built into the xv6 kernel in labs. In English.

main.title: Linux Kernel Internals: Processes
main.why: From LinuxThreads to NPTL, then task_struct, the process lifecycle, fork and context switches. In Mandarin.

main.title: A fork() in the road
main.why: Argues fork is a 1970s hack that now hurts thread safety, security and scalability, and proposes alternatives.
One blocking task stalls a whole event loop, so some work belongs back on threads.

main.title: Linux Kernel Internals: CPU Scheduler
main.why: From the 2.4 and O(1) schedulers through CFS to EEVDF and sched_ext, plus load balancing and PREEMPT_RT. In Mandarin.

main.title: An EEVDF CPU scheduler for Linux
main.why: EEVDF replaced CFS in 6.6, adding virtual deadlines so latency-sensitive tasks run sooner.

main.title: Avoiding CPU Throttling in a Containerized Environment
main.why: CFS quotas throttled multi-threaded services past 100 ms. Pinning cores with cpusets halved P99 and saved 11% of cores.

main.title: ghOSt: Fast & Flexible User-Space Delegation of Linux Scheduling
main.why: Scheduling decisions delegated to userspace agents, so new policies ship without changing the kernel.

main.title: Modernizing the Meta Ads Service With an Open-Source Kernel Scheduler
main.why: EEVDF regressed ads latency, so Meta wrote a sched_ext policy that splits CPUs into latency-critical and background pools.

main.title: Linux Kernel Internals: Synchronization
main.why: Spinlocks, semaphores, rwlocks, MCS locks and seqlocks, and why locks limit scalability. In Mandarin.

main.title: MCS locks and qspinlocks
main.why: Contended spinlocks bounce one cache line across CPUs. MCS queues let each waiter spin on its own, the basis of qspinlock.

main.title: What is RCU, Fundamentally?
main.why: Readers run alongside an updater without locks, and old versions are freed only after existing readers finish.

main.title: Multi-generational LRU: the next generation
main.why: Replaces the active and inactive page lists with generations and reclaims from the oldest, merged in 6.1.

main.title: TMO: Transparent Memory Offloading in Datacenters
main.why: PSI measures work lost to memory shortage, which decides how much cold memory to move to compressed RAM or SSD.

main.title: TPP: Transparent Page Placement for CXL-Enabled Tiered-Memory
main.why: Keeps hot pages in local DRAM and demotes cold ones to slower CXL memory, mostly merged in 5.18.
One HashMap resize held the mmap_lock for writing and stalled every thread's page faults for 15 seconds.

main.title: The multiqueue block layer
main.why: One request queue could not keep up with SSDs, so blk-mq splits submission into per-CPU and per-hardware queues.

main.title: Ringing in a new asynchronous I/O API
main.why: Why AIO fell short, and how io_uring passes requests and results through rings shared with the kernel.

main.title: I/O Passthru: Upstreaming a flexible and efficient I/O Path in Linux
main.why: NVMe commands go through io_uring and a char device instead of the block layer, now in mainline.

main.title: Linux Kernel Internals: File Systems
main.why: Files and descriptors in the universal I/O model, then I/O multiplexing with select and epoll. In Mandarin.
Disk reads and open() block an event loop even with O_NONBLOCK, so they moved to a thread pool.

main.title: PostgreSQL's fsync() surprise
main.why: When writeback fails, the kernel can drop the dirty pages and fsync may never report the error.

main.title: File Systems Unfit as Distributed Storage Backends: Lessons from 10 Years of Ceph Evolution
main.why: Building on local file systems cost Ceph in transactions and metadata, so BlueStore writes to raw devices.

main.title: KVM: Linux Virtualization Infrastructure
main.why: How KVM and virtio work, read through a minimal KVM host, and what KVM gained since 6.6. In Mandarin.

main.title: Firecracker: Lightweight Virtualization for Serverless Applications
main.why: A minimal virtual machine monitor that gives serverless workloads VM isolation with container-like overhead.
Containers running systemd escaped their cgroup limits until the runtime used the systemd cgroup driver.

main.title: Understanding Host Network Stack Overheads
main.why: At 100 Gbps one core can no longer keep up, and copying data to the application becomes the main cost.
Tuning from the NIC, CPU affinity and NUMA up through TCP pacing, congestion control and sysctls.

main.title: The eXpress Data Path: Fast Programmable Packet Processing in the Operating System Kernel
main.why: XDP. Verified BPF programs run in the network driver and handle packets before the kernel network stack.

main.title: Open-sourcing Katran, a scalable network load balancer
main.why: The load balancer moved from the IPVS kernel module to XDP and BPF, handling packets right after the NIC.

main.title: The eBPF Runtime in the Linux Kernel
main.why: How programs are verified, compiled and attached to kernel hooks, and what eBPF is used for today.

main.title: Strobelight: A profiling service built on open source technology
main.why: Fleet-wide profilers built on eBPF. One fix they surfaced saved an estimated 15,000 servers a year.

main.title: drgn: How the Linux Kernel Team at Meta Debugs the Kernel at Scale
main.why: A debugger scripted in Python that inspects a running kernel or a core dump.
